scopeReview: SPS-7.D.1–3: changing women’s economic roles, participation versus wage/opportunity equity and microloan opportunities with context. Explicit treatment of unpaid work and multiscale barriers.
varietyReview: Four assessed original stimuli: labor-force denominators, average hourly earnings chart, unpaid-care time and nonrandom loan-study income changes. Additional questions examine transport/education, enterprise conditions and spatial variation.
repetitionReview: Distinct participation, earnings, time and evaluation measures; no conflation of a workforce share with participation, an unadjusted gap with identical-work discrimination or a before/after loan change with proven causation. Detailed options, varied keys, uncalibrated difficulty.
referenceNote: Official framework and primary index scope checked. All records and examples hypothetical/original, reported statistical categories not a claim to capture all gender identities. No personal credit/eligibility advice, copied content or independent human review.

questions.independentReview: Independent ratios.6/.8 andgap.2. Record uses two reported statistical categories, not a claim all gender identities or unpaid work are captured; laborforce not equal employed.

questions.correctOption: The ratio rises from 80% to 90%, but the later average earnings remain unequal.
questions.independentReview: Recomputed ratios.8/.9,absolutegaps20/10. Hourly averages comparable; not an adjusted equal-pay estimate or proof of a single discriminatory mechanism.

questions.correctOption: Women average 10 more unpaid-care hours per week, which can constrain access to paid opportunities unless other conditions offset the burden.
questions.independentReview: Independently20−10=10hours. Categories meanreportedcaretime, not totalwork/timebudget; no assumption allwomen/men share identical roles or causalityproved.

questions.correctOption: Participants gained 40 and the comparison group 30; the 10-unit difference in changes is descriptive without stronger design evidence.

questions.correctOption: Wages, job security, advancement, working conditions and unpaid burdens may remain unequal.
questions.independentReview: Direct SPS-7.D.2: participation versus equity; no claim every workplace gap has one cause or allwomen share one experience.

questions.correctOption: They can expand skills and reachable work options, while institutions, care responsibilities and labor demand still shape outcomes.
